title: POC acceptance rulebook signoff & deliverables — Clearview Financial
summary: Final signoff on POC acceptance thresholds and delivery artifacts. Agreed go/no-go metrics across accuracy, latency p50/p95, throughput, and cost targets. Confirmed reporting format: CSV of raw runs + aggregated JSON summary + annotated slide deck + short demo video. 4-week POC timeline confirmed with weekly checkpoints. Action items: Redwood to run initial baseline within 5 business days, customer to provide 5k-sample eval set and SSO/KMS access details.

transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-04-02
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE); Diego Ramos (Redwood SE); Priya Patel (Redwood CSM); Liam O'Neal (Clearview Head of ML); Sophia Grant (Platform Eng); Rajiv Menon (Security); Emily Park (PM)

Auto-summary: Final POC acceptance signoff; established quantitative go/no-go thresholds and deliverable formats; agreed 4-week timeline and owners.

[00:00] Maya Chen: All right everyone, thanks for joining — uh — appreciate you squeezing this in. the goal today is to lock the acceptance rulebook, the go-nogo thresholds, and what we'll hand back as deliverables at the end of the POC.
[00:18] Liam O'Neal: Yep, sounds good. We're primarily focused on intent extraction and fraud-rerank pipelines for this POC, so those are the slices we'll evaluate.
[00:28] Diego Ramos: Great, thanks. I'll walk through the baseline metrics we expect to capture and the reporting artifacts. Quick note — some of the terms may be a little messy in auto transcript, k-v cache sometimes comes out like K-V cash in our notes, so we'll try to be explicit.
[00:40] Emily Park: One ask up front, we want the acceptance tests to be reproducible. So a list of commands, runbook, and the raw logs are mandatory.
[00:50] Maya Chen: Absolutely. Our recommended deliverables: 1) raw CSV of every inference run with seeds and input hashes, 2) an aggregated JSON summary with p50/p95 latency and token counts, 3) annotated slide deck with key findings and screenshots, 4) a short video of the acceptance demo, and 5) the runbook (commands + env). Any objections?
[01:12] Rajiv Menon: No objections, but on the security side we need to ensure the logs don't contain PII and that any keys are rotated. We'll need the KMS integration details — our infra team uses a customer-managed KMS.
[01:24] Priya Patel: Noted, Rajiv. Redwood supports KMS/HSM integrations, we'll include the network diagrams and SOC2 summary along with the runbook.
[01:33] Sophia Grant: For workload sizing — our peak is about 200 RPS for inference across two endpoints, average prompt length ~120 tokens. For the POC though, we want a stress window at 300 RPS for 10 minutes to validate autoscale behavior.
[01:48] Diego Ramos: That's helpful. So we'll capture both steady-state and stress tests. Proposed throughput acceptance: steady-state at 200 RPS sustained for 30 minutes with p50 latency < 120ms and p95 < 650ms, and stress test tolerance: system stays available and error rate under 1.5% at 300 RPS during the 10-min window.
[02:07] Liam O'Neal: Those latency numbers feel optimistic but possible. What about quality metrics for intent extraction? We need accuracy and false positive thresholds.
[02:16] Maya Chen: Right — for intent extraction we propose: macro-F1 >= 0.92 on the eval set, precision on top intents >= 0.9, and hallucination / irrelevant response rate < 3% measured on a 1k stratified sample. Go/no-go: if any of those fall below the thresholds by more than 2 absolute points, it's a fail unless agreed mitigation reduces risk.
[02:38] Emily Park: How are we measuring hallucinations? The rubric needs to be explicit.
[02:42] Diego Ramos: Good point. We'll provide an annotation schema — binary labels per response (correct/incorrect/irrelevant), and an example pack. Hallucination rate = count(irrelevant or fabricated) / total annotated. We'll also include a small human review panel for adjudication (3 reviewers, majority vote).
[02:59] Sophia Grant: On cost targets — we want to estimate per-1000-token cost. Can Redwood provide an expected cost envelope?
[03:06] Maya Chen: We'll produce a cost model in the runbook: tokens in/out, GPU-hours for runs, and an estimated $/1k tokens for the chosen model variant. For the acceptance we propose a target of <$0.50 per 1k user-visible tokens during baseline runs; if we see spikes above $0.9 per 1k we mark it red.
[03:24] Rajiv Menon: Also log retention and audit — we need immutable audit logs for all inference requests for 90 days. Is that doable in the POC?
[03:31] Priya Patel: Yes, we can enable extended retention for logs during the POC. We'll provide sample audit records and the retention policy.
[03:39] [04:00] Speaker 1 (Liam?): Okay, timeline — can we walk through week-by-week?
[04:07] Diego Ramos: Sure. Week 0 (this week) — final signoff on criteria and runbook. Week 1 — integration and smoke tests (env setup, creds, KMS). Week 2 — baseline runs and initial quality evals. Week 3 — performance tuning (batching, quantization suggestions), and rerun benchmarks. Week 4 — acceptance runs and delivery of artifacts + final demo.
[04:28] Liam O'Neal: That fits our calendar. We prefer the acceptance window week of April 20th.
[04:34] Maya Chen: Noted. So acceptance run targeted for 2026-04-20 to 2026-04-24.
[04:39] Emily Park: On reporting format, we want both machine-readable and an executive-friendly one. The JSON summary you mentioned plus a one-page SLI dashboard PDF would be ideal.
[04:49] Maya Chen: We'll produce both. The JSON will include latencies, error rates, token counts, model version, seed, commit hash, and environment metadata. The PDF will be a one-pager with the go/no-go pass/fail and supporting charts.
[04:59] Sophia Grant: For the models — we agreed to try the open Llama-variants and a quantized Redwood-recommended variant. If capacity becomes an issue, what's the fallback?
[05:08] Diego Ramos: We'll configure a fallback policy — route to a slightly smaller quantized model for tail traffic. We'll publish the exact variants in the runbook. Note that fallbacks will be flagged in the final report as they affect accuracy targets.
[05:20] [06:00] Rajiv Menon: Compliance — we'll need SAML SSO connection details and a statement of data processing. Also, can you confirm encryption-at-rest for both cache and model weights in Private deployments?
[06:12] Priya Patel: For Private deployments yes, AES-256 at rest and optional HSM-backed keys with customer-managed KMS. We'll include the architecture diagram and the encryption statements in the security packet.
[06:24] Liam O'Neal: Quick question — how are retries and timeouts configured for the SDK? We want to ensure client-side timeouts don't distort latency numbers.
[06:33] Diego Ramos: We'll standardize the client config for benchmark runs: single retry policy disabled, 30s overall request timeout, and explicit connection pooling settings. We'll include the curl-like commands in the runbook so your infra can reproduce.
[06:46] Maya Chen: Let's talk reporting cadence. We'll do weekly status with a short CSV of recent runs and a mid-week summary slide. The final artifact bundle will include a CSV, JSON summary, deck, demo video link, and a reproducible runbook.
[07:01] Emily Park: Make sure the CSV includes input_hash, prompt_tokens, output_tokens, model_variant, latency_ms, error_flag.
[07:07] Diego Ramos: Will do.
[07:10] [08:00] Speaker 2 (Sophia): On evaluation slices — we want stratification by intent type and by prompt length bucket: short (<50 tokens), medium (50-200), long (>200).
[08:19] Maya Chen: Agreed. We'll publish slice definitions and include breakdowns in the summary JSON.
[08:26] Liam O'Neal: One more on acceptance thresholds: If p95 latency is slightly above target but accuracy is well above, is remediation path allowed?
[08:36] Maya Chen: We defined an escalation policy: if one metric misses but others are green and there is an actionable remediation with a committed timeline, we mark as conditional pass and agree on a post-POC follow-up. But the core go/no-go will prioritize quality first, then latency, then cost.
[08:53] [09:30] Diego Ramos: Small caveat — for fairness in measurement, we need the customer to run warmup sequences before measuring to populate KV cache. Otherwise cold-starts will inflate p95.
[09:41] Sophia Grant: We'll run the warmup script you provide. Also, please document the KV cache behavior — we saw it referred to as K-V cash in one of your earlier notes — so clarity is appreciated.
[09:52] Maya Chen: Noted. We'll be explicit.
[10:00] [10:45] Rajiv Menon: For the log-sharing, we need a secure S3 bucket with restricted IAM roles. Can Redwood push logs there or do you need push vs pull?
[10:55] Priya Patel: We can push to your bucket if you set the appropriate write role and we will encrypt in transit. We'll include the bucket policy template.
[11:04] Liam O'Neal: Are we capturing tokenization differences? Some of our baselines use a custom tokenizer and that might shift token counts.
[11:11] Diego Ramos: We'll capture the tokenizer version and the token counts as seen by the model. If you want, we can also store raw byte-lengths.
[11:18] Emily Park: One more deliverable item — can you include a short sensitivity analysis showing how accuracy changes with quantization?
[11:26] Diego Ramos: Yes. We'll include a quantization sensitivity section with delta-accuracy and CPU/GPU savings.
[11:33] [12:00] Speaker label noise: Speaker 1: uh mm-hmm
[12:07] Maya Chen: Ok timecheck — we're about halfway. Anything critical we haven't covered?
[12:12] Liam O'Neal: No, I think we covered the main pieces.
[12:16] Maya Chen: Great. Now the exact go/no-go thresholds that we agreed on — I'll read them aloud so they're on the record:
[12:23] Maya Chen: 1) Intent extraction macro-F1 >= 0.92; 2) Precision (top intents) >= 0.90; 3) Hallucination < 3% on annotated sample; 4) Steady-state p50 < 120ms, p95 < 650ms at 200 RPS; 5) Stress 300 RPS 10-min window with error rate < 1.5%; 6) Cost per 1k visible tokens < $0.50 baseline (red if > $0.9). If two or more thresholds fail, outcome = fail. If one threshold fails but there's a documented remediation plan accepted by both parties, outcome = conditional pass.
[13:01] Sophia Grant: We accept those thresholds — will sign off once we get the written runbook and data requirements.
[13:07] Emily Park: Ditto.
[13:10] Rajiv Menon: Security contingent on KMS/HSM confirmation and review of architecture diagram.
[13:16] Priya Patel: We'll get those to you by Monday.
[13:20] [14:00] Diego Ramos: A few notes on reporting format specifics: CSV columns — timestamp, input_hash, user_id (anonymized), prompt_tokens, response_tokens, latency_ms, http_status, model_variant, commit_hash. JSON summary — nested arrays we'll flatten to arrays in the file but the summary file will be a single JSON object with strings and numbers.
[14:37] Liam O'Neal: Ok. About demos — can we have a short live-run during the final acceptance meeting?
[14:43] Maya Chen: Yes, the final demo will include a one-click replay of a set of 50 golden prompts plus the live run. We'll record it for audit.
[14:52] [15:30] Speaker 3 (Emily): One last logistics thing — who signs the acceptance? Is it product or security?
[15:36] Maya Chen: Typically product (Emily or Liam) signs on acceptance of functional metrics, and security (Rajiv) signs off on compliance artifacts. We'll allow both signatures in the acceptance PDF.
[15:46] Liam O'Neal: Fine by me.
[15:49] [16:00] Priya Patel: Action items recap — I'll paste those into the calendar invite after the call.
[16:06] Maya Chen: Great. Any other outstanding blockers?
[16:10] Sophia Grant: Not from infra side, just timeline alignment which is fine.
[16:14] Rajiv Menon: I'll look for the security packet.
[16:18] Maya Chen: Perfect. Thanks everyone — we'll circulate the runbook and S3 policy templates by Monday.
[16:24] [17:00] Diego Ramos: I'll coordinate the benchmark window and send the test creds to Sophia in a secure channel.
[17:08] Maya Chen: Okay meeting adjourned. Thanks all.

Recap (verbatim for notes):
- POC length: 4 weeks; acceptance window: 2026-04-20 to 2026-04-24.
- Go/No-go thresholds: accuracy, hallucination, latency p50/p95, error rates, cost per 1k tokens.
- Deliverable bundle: raw CSV, aggregated JSON summary, annotated deck, demo recording, runbook, security packet.
- Next steps & action owners listed in action_items above.

References mentioned: benchmark runbook link (to be shared), SOC2 summary (attached later), S3 bucket policy template (will be provided).
